clearedSpotChecks.check: evm2 main past 7c9f3b6d (the commit tempo main pins for the next release): do the rewritten DIV and MOD handlers, the new word to address conversion and the EXP gas change compute what the specification and the PoolManager need?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched crates/evm2/src/interpreter/instructions/arithmetic.rs at 7c9f3b6deb23005fc84596ba1b13a6492d942014 and at main. The only differences are lines 22 and 32: 'if b.is_zero() { Word::ZERO } else { a.wrapping_div(*b) }' became 'a.checked_div(*b).unwrap_or_default()', and the same for rem. In ruint-1.21.1.crate from static.crates.io, checked_div and checked_rem return None only for a zero divisor and otherwise call Div and Rem (src/div.rs lines 9-14 and 36-41), and impl_bin_op maps Div and Rem to wrapping_div and wrapping_rem (lines 149-150); byte_len is bit_len().div_ceil(8) (src/bits.rs lines 330-332). So DIV and MOD by zero still give zero, which src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol and the divisions in src/libraries/FullMath.sol rely on. SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, EXP and SIGNEXTEND are textually unchanged. I did not re-read the alloy-primitives From<U256> for B256 conversion; the release that endpoints run does not contain this code yet.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Reruns on 2026-11-27 of battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py and replay.py on tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 and on rpc.mainnet.arc.io (v0.8.6-rc1, 37812c61), plus the same sets on arc.drpc.org and arc-rpc.publicnode.com.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I wrote my own vector set rather than reuse the unit's scripts: 1,200 operand triples built from 19 edge values (0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 31, 32, 255, 256, 2^128 and 2^128-1, 2^160-1, 2^255 and its neighbours, 2^256-1 and 2^256-2, the secp256k1 field prime, 2^192+12345) against six moduli, each run through DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, EXP, SIGNEXTEND, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, BYTE, SHL, SHR and SAR in a state-override contract by eth_call at latest. The results were checked against a Python reference: 19,200 of 19,200 equal on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz (web3_clientVersion tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748) and 19,200 of 19,200 on https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io once rate limit errors were retried at a slower pace. arc_getVersion queried by me gives v0.8.6-rc1 37812c61 on rpc.mainnet.arc.io, v0.8.6 8e8edb7a on arc.drpc.org and v0.8.5 602eed3b on arc-rpc.publicnode.com (reth/v2.2.0-508cbdf), as the unit states. battery.log shows 99,985 of 99,985 with 0 mismatches on both chains.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-1175: which builds answer the Arc endpoints, does the value-call frame hook of F-125 differ between them, and can a test set be pinned to one build?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched crates/evm/src/evm.rs at arc-node tags v0.8.5 and v0.8.6, and both hash to sha256 1ce0d1e6a2088df29e641518edd80c0772ede5233508220ba99961823c66bb45, as the unit states. The frame hook (lines 226-227, 428-451, 515-516) adds the EIP-7708 transfer log and checks a native USDC blocklist kept in the native coin control precompile's storage. Only the USDC issuer's blocklist role can make a native payout from src/types/Currency.sol:48 fail. That hazard needs an issuer and is already recorded as F-125. An ordinary account cannot put an address on the blocklist, so the unprivileged scope does not change. The two unpublished commits behind rpc.mainnet.arc.io and arc.drpc.org cannot be read, so the claim that they share this file rests on the identical test results and not on source.
